# Julius autonomous landing (founder-governed directory)

Everything in this directory, and `.github/workflows/julius-land.yml`, is founder-governed: the lander refuses to land any PR that touches it. The main-provenance gate and the module it imports are also hard-forbidden by PREFIX, case-insensitively: any path starting with `scripts/julius-main-provenance` or `scripts/julius-review-currency` (the `.mjs`, `.d.mts`, test, and any sibling name). An autonomous landing can never change what the gate trusts. The same prefix rule covers the gate and secret-handling scripts that workflows run: `scripts/julius-main-monotonicity`, `scripts/julius-paid-slot`, `scripts/julius-subscription-check`, `scripts/julius-live-preflight-gates`, `scripts/julius-accept`, `scripts/relay-repository-boundary`, `scripts/export-julius-harness`, `.github/julius-live-` (the `julius-live-*.sh` boundary scripts and helpers), `.github/actions/`, `.github/julius-mission-slice/` and `.github/julius-learning-registrations/` and `scripts/julius-landing` (the landing system's own tests, `scripts/julius-landing*.test.ts`). `relay-bridge/**`, `src/**`, the mission directories (`.github/julius-missions/**`), `JULIUS_HARNESS_MANIFEST.md` and every other path stay allowed.

## Checkpoint attestation (installer-1)

The live gates trust a signed `JULIUS-CHECKPOINT-V1` file at `.github/julius-landing/checkpoints/<checkpoint>.txt` with a sibling `.sig`. `HARD_FORBIDDEN_PATH` matches that directory, and so does the provenance gate's byte copy of the same expression, so no App pull request can add or swap one. Accept-main compares those files to `HEAD` and the verifier compares every trusted file to the hashes inside the signed text.

These gates require that attestation to be on main already, so they cannot land the first one. The founder installer-1 commit is made outside the lander. Its parent is the attested checkpoint. That commit lands this verifier together with the attestation file and its `.sig`. There is no bypass flag, and the first run does not trust an unsigned tree. Do not squash that commit onto an older main: the named checkpoint would not be an ancestor and the gate fails closed.

RECOVERY: no signed checkpoint attestation is on main. The founder installer-1 commit lands this verifier and .github/julius-landing/checkpoints/<checkpoint>.txt together with its .sig, in one governed commit whose parent is the attested checkpoint, outside the lander. There is no bypass and the first run does not trust an unsigned tree.

The commits after checkpoint `10aedd11643a1d717311b5824d54e863aa94d763` on the provenance branch are that installer lineage, not signed landings. Each of them touches only the trusted computing base, the checkpoint attestation files, or an exact companion path (this README, `docs/provenance/checkpoint-2528ac5c-f539cab2.unsigned.txt`, and the four landing/trust test files). There is no wildcard. None of them carries a landing block or a `.sig`. The founder bootstrap regenerates the attestation so its trusted-file hashes name the tree that contains these fixes, signs that text, and commits the `.txt` and the `.sig`. The pinned reviewer key is not changed here. Until that signature exists, `requireTrustedVerifier` fails closed. After it exists, the checkpoint plus this lineage covers the branch. The next commit on main has to be a signed `JULIUS-CLEARANCE-V1` landing: pinned key, repo `ohdieyuh-glitch/sunday-relay`, tree equal to the landing commit's tree, base equal to its single parent, head the cleared commit, inside the clearance's validity window (at most 24 hours), nonce unused on the first-parent chain. A landing older than its clearance is not a live authorization. Fold it into a later signed checkpoint, moving the checkpoint sha forward, before the clearance expires, or the gate fails closed.

Operation: the Independent Reviewer signs a clearance (`reviewer-tools.mjs sign`), MAIN JULIUS dispatches `Julius land` with the clearance and signature. The job verifies the clearance, waits for CI, then performs ONE FINAL READ (PR, files, bot-comment digest, main's tip and the whole CI state, all paginated fail-closed) and decides from that read alone. `dry_run` defaults to true; only the exact string `false` lands.

## How a landing happens (no merge endpoint)

The lander does NOT use `PUT /pulls/N/merge` (it pins only the PR head, not the base). It uses the git data API:

1. `POST /repos/{r}/git/commits` with `tree` = the cleared tree, `parents` = `[the cleared base]`, `message` = the landing commit message below, `author` = `committer` = `julius-lander[bot] <347026632+julius-lander[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. The App id is 5444986. That write uses the lander App token, not the workflow token.
2. Read the created commit back (`GET /repos/{r}/commits/{sha}`) and require: the cleared tree, exactly one parent which is the cleared base, the exact message (GitHub stores a created commit's message without its ONE final newline: that single difference is accepted, nothing else), the bot identity. The head commit of the PR must likewise carry a RESOLVED top-level GitHub author account equal to `julius-worker[bot]` (an unresolved author is refused: the main-provenance gate judges exactly that login). Every error text the lander prints is redacted for tokens and Authorization headers.
3. SPEND THE CLEARANCE: `POST /repos/{r}/git/refs` with `{ "ref": "refs/tags/julius-landing-nonce-<nonce>", "sha": <created> }`. Creating a ref is atomic and GitHub answers 422 if it exists, so two uses of one clearance cannot both pass. This is the durable one-use record: main's history alone cannot be it, because a landing is a child of the base and a main reset to the base would make the clearance look unused. Step 2 of the job also READS this tag first (404 is the only "unspent" answer; a spent tag refuses even if the nonce is no longer in the scanned history window; a dry run only reads it). Order: AFTER the created commit was read back (a failed or lying creation spends nothing) and BEFORE the ref update (the use is recorded before its effect, so a failure after this step fails closed). **A refusal after the tag exists spends the clearance: the reviewer signs a new clearance with a new nonce.** The tag is never moved or deleted by the lander. **The tag is a durable record, NOT tamper-proof:** the worker App that creates it could also delete or re-create it (deleting it would un-spend a clearance, creating one in advance would refuse a clearance); a repository ruleset on `refs/tags/julius-landing-nonce-*` (a founder-only repository setting) is the control that closes this, and until it exists this one-use guarantee rests on the worker App not misbehaving.
4. `PATCH /repos/{r}/git/refs/heads/main` with `{ "sha": <created>, "force": false }`. A non-forced ref update is a FAST-FORWARD TEST, not an equality compare-and-swap: GitHub accepts it iff the new commit is a fast-forward of main's value at that instant. It therefore refuses a main that moved forward or sideways after the lander's last tip read, but it ACCEPTS a main that was reset BACKWARD to an ancestor of the cleared base between that read and the call (the rollback is undone, nothing here can tell; a residual, no REST parameter closes it). What the post-update read does detect: main is no longer the created commit (someone moved it again): ALERT, exit 2. What it cannot detect, and does not need to: "main is the created commit but its parent is not the cleared base" cannot occur, because the sha names the content and the read-back checked tree and parent before the call, so main == created commit implies parent == base by construction. Any failure refuses and reports; there is never a retry and never `force`. Only a clean HTTP 4xx answer (other than 408 and 429) counts as "GitHub refused and main did not move". On ANY other outcome (timeout, 5xx, network error, an unreadable answer) the update may have been applied with its answer lost, so the lander re-reads main's tip: main == the created commit is treated as landed (`LANDED (the PATCH response was lost)`, then the post-checks); main == the cleared base is an ALERT, exit 2 (the request may still be applied late, so the state is in doubt; no retry, no comment, the PR stays open, and the clearance is spent); anything else is an ALERT (exit 2) naming the tip. If the tip cannot be re-read the job also exits 2. Every request has a 30-second deadline, so a connection that hangs after an applied update ends in this recovery re-read; a request that timed out could still be applied late, so after the ALERT that main is still the cleared base, check main again before signing anything new (the clearance is spent in any case).
5. Comment on the PR naming the landed commit, then close it. **The PR will show as CLOSED, not MERGED**: the landed commit is not the PR head. That is expected.

A dry run performs every read and every check and computes the commit body, but sends no write at all (no commit, no nonce tag, no ref update, no comment, no close; it only READS whether the nonce tag exists and refuses if it does); it prints what the live run would send, including the full landing commit message.

## The landing commit message (format "JULIUS LANDING v1")

The one definition is `buildLandingCommitMessage` / `parseLandingCommitMessage` in `land-lib.mjs`; the specification for other implementers (the provenance gate) is:

```
<free text: subject, blank line, body>
<blank line>
-----BEGIN JULIUS LANDING-----
v: 1
clearance-nonce: <32 hex, equal to the clearance's nonce>
clearance-b64: <standard base64 (RFC 4648 section 4, alphabet A-Za-z0-9+/, padded), ONE line, of the EXACT signed clearance text bytes>
signature-b64: <standard base64, padded, ONE line, of the 64-byte ed25519 signature over those exact bytes>
-----END JULIUS LANDING-----
```

- The block is the FINAL lines of the message; one trailing newline after the END line, nothing after it.
- Exactly one BEGIN and one END marker; each marker is a whole line. The uppercase phrase `JULIUS LANDING` appears EXACTLY TWICE in the whole message, once in each marker line, and nowhere else: the free text must not contain it at all (a reader that counts mentions answers indeterminate otherwise); lower and mixed case, such as "Julius landing", is fine. The parser rejects any other count, and the lander refuses to build such a message; the lander's own free text is built from the PR number, head, kind and dates only, never the PR title).
- Exactly the four keys above, in that order, each once, no extras; values on one line; base64 must be canonical (decode and re-encode gives the same text).
- The clearance text is the `JULIUS-CLEARANCE-V1` text (see `parseClearance`). **The PR number, head, tree and base are read ONLY from the signed clearance text**, never from free text. The block nonce must equal the clearance nonce.
- A reader verifies the signature against the reviewer key committed at the landed commit's PARENT (the tree the landing was authorized under), then requires: clearance `tree` == the landed commit's tree, clearance `base` == the landed commit's single parent, and the clearance `head` is a worker-authored commit.

## Facts to remember

- A ref update made with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN triggers NO further workflows. Accept-main, the hold check, ledger rows and paid dispatch are run by MAIN JULIUS after each landing, as before.
- Exit codes. 0 = landed (or a dry run that passed). 1 = REFUSED, nothing landed; this includes ANY unexpected error before the ref update is sent, which ends with ONE `REFUSED: unexpected error before anything was landed: ...` line, never a stack trace. 2 = ALERT: main is not the created commit after the update, the read of main after the update failed (`ALERT AFTER LANDING: main was updated to <sha> but ...`, the PR comment and close are still attempted), the outcome of an ambiguous update was the cleared base (state in doubt: the request may still be applied late; the clearance is spent) or neither the created commit nor the base, or any unexpected error after the ref update was sent; it is never exit 1 once the update may have applied. 3 = the commit LANDED but the PR comment or the PR close failed (each is attempted on its own; do them by hand). An ALERT is not an undo.
- `required-checks.txt`: one check per line, `Name` or `Name @15368`. With `@id` the single check run of that name must also have been produced by that GitHub App id (15368 = GitHub Actions), so a look-alike check from another app cannot stand in for the real job. **Any other consumer of this file must strip the ` @<digits>` suffix** (a line such as `Verify Relay @15368` names the check `Verify Relay`); the lander's own `parseRequiredChecks` in `land-lib.mjs` is the only reader today (the workflow, `reviewer-tools.mjs` and the repository's other scripts do not read it), and anything new should call that function rather than re-parse the lines; the first live dry run proves the ids. Only the conclusion `success` is green: `neutral` and `skipped` are refused. Manual rollback of a landing: `git revert <landed sha>` through the normal founder-governed path, then accept-main at the revert commit.
- The GitHub App `julius-worker` must NOT have the `workflows` permission; the founder confirms this when installing, and the permission list is recorded in the installing PR.
- The reviewer's key: only the PUBLIC key is committed (`reviewer-ed25519.pub`). A placeholder is refused until the reviewer replaces it.
- `governed-exceptions` in a clearance lets the reviewer permit a change to `scripts/julius-live-contract-check.mjs` (spend ceilings) or `relay-bridge/julius/role-effort.test.ts` (effort tripwire) for one PR; every other governed path is refused with or without a clearance.
- The digest of bot comments, inline comments and reviews covers, per row, the author, id, the edit timestamp (`updated_at`, else `created_at`; `submitted_at` for a review) and `sha256(body)`. A clearance signed under the earlier digest (no body, no timestamp for reviews) no longer matches: the reviewer re-runs `reviewer-tools.mjs digest` and signs a new clearance.
- A refused or failed landing can leave the created commit as an unreferenced git object (the commit is created before main is touched). That residue is harmless: nothing points at it, and the ref update is the ONLY thing that lands a change.
- The landed commit has no CI of its own (it is a new commit on main with the cleared, already-checked tree); the checks that count are those on the cleared head.

## Operator runbook (lessons from the first live landings, 2026-10-19)

1. The human at the installer prompt is the only gate in a founder-run install: paste the reviewer's signed G6 token for that exact head. The prompt does not take a PR number. The token is bound to the repository, the PR, the head, the tree, the base, the bot-item count and a digest of the full text of every comment, inline comment and review, and it is valid at most two hours. The installer verifies it against the reviewer key committed in this directory (already fingerprint-checked on the clone). After the token verifies, the installer re-reads everything the token was issued for; any change stops the install.
2. A dry run cannot show real-GitHub behaviour. GitHub stores a created commit message without its final newline (the lander accepts exactly the sent message or the sent message minus its one final newline). Treat every write path as NOT PROVEN until rehearsed on real GitHub.
3. The five real-infra checks come from `julius-real-infra.yml`. Its path filter now covers the paths the landing steps touch; if a PR still lacks them, run `gh workflow run julius-real-infra.yml --ref <pr branch>` (the checks must be GitHub Actions, app 15368, on the PR head, once each).
4. A late bot comment (Vercel, Codex) invalidates the signed bot digest. Wait for the Vercel comment and commit status before asking for the digest, and run dry_run=true and dry_run=false back to back, re-reading the bot items between.
5. A transient infrastructure failure (Docker Hub 502) is diagnosed from the job logs; `gh run rerun --failed` on the same head is allowed. A clean Codex review on one head does not carry to the next; unresolved Codex findings are blocking and are reproduced first.
6. Supersede means close the PR and delete its branch: the open script pushes only to an absent branch. A landed branch is retired before its allowlisted name is reused; the allowlist is not extended for re-cuts.
7. A network error after a write is neither success nor failure: re-read the state independently. An unreadable `git ls-remote` is UNKNOWN, never absence.
8. Run founder-credential scripts by pasting the bash command into Git Bash. Do not wrap them in PowerShell, and do not route around the permission classifier.
9. The host clock can be about 80 s behind GitHub: order events against GitHub timestamps.
10. Any fixture with an expiry needs the clock pin used in the landing suites; long end-to-end cases carry an explicit test timeout.

## Output redaction (what the job's printed text hides, and what it does not)
Every printed line goes through one redactor. Each statement below is a probe run on the real `redact()` (tests sweep the shapes character by character and pin the residuals). It hides:
- **The job token itself**, matched character by character: its literal text; with whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks) between any of its characters; and with ANY of its ASCII characters written as a percent escape (a single-byte `%XX`; a non-ASCII character is not matched as a UTF-8 escape): each character is matched as itself OR as its `%XX` escape (upper or lower hex, in any mix, also escaped again as `%25XX`, up to three levels), so a fully, partly or singly percent-encoded token is hidden, also with whitespace between characters; a LINE BREAK (LF or CRLF, then at most one space or tab) is also accepted INSIDE an escape: between the `%` and its hex digits, between the two digits and between the `25` levels.
- **The job token in base64** (alone, behind `x-access-token:`, before `:x-oauth-basic`, at the three byte alignments), except about four characters of the tail; also when the base64 text is WRAPPED by a line break (LF or CRLF, then at most one space or tab) at any width, when its `=` `+` `/` are percent-encoded, and in the base64url alphabet (`-` `_`).
- **GitHub token shapes** (`ghs_`, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`, any credential of that shape, not only the job token) followed by 16 to 255 letters and digits (`github_pat_`: also underscores): in plain form; with any character written as a percent escape (`ghs%5F...`, `%67%68%73%5F...`, `%25XX` up to three levels); and with a LINE BREAK (LF or CRLF, then at most one space or tab) between ANY two of its characters (between the prefix letters, before and after an underscore, anywhere in the body, any number of breaks), and the same break is accepted inside a `%XX` escape of a shape (between the `%` and its hex digits, between the two digits, between the `25` levels). A shape is recognised wherever it starts (behind letters, digits, an underscore or an escaped newline such as `%0A`; a word that merely contains `ghs_` plus 16 letters is over-redacted on purpose), and a run never continues into the head of another shape, so a second token on the next line, or glued to the first, is hidden as its own token. A PLAIN space is NOT a gap: a foreign shape split by a plain space is printed (below), and the words after a whole token survive.
- **`Bearer <x>`** (any case; an optional `:` or `=`; the value may be quoted) **and `Authorization: <x>`** (any case; `:` or `=`): a QUOTED value (JSON or single quotes) is hidden alone with its quotes kept; any other value hides the REST OF THE LINE (a scheme word such as Bearer, Basic, Negotiate or Digest, a value with spaces, `;` or `,`), so what follows `Authorization:` on that line is over-redacted on purpose. A quoted value may contain escaped quotes; a `Bearer` value in backslash-escaped quotes (a backslash before each quote, double or single, as in JSON inside JSON) is hidden whole, quotes included: the closing run of backslashes must equal the opening one, so an escaped quote of a deeper level inside the value does not end it, and an unterminated escaped quote hides the rest of the line (v3.5h); an unterminated quote hides the rest of the line; a FOLDED header with an unquoted value (continuation lines that start with a space or tab) is hidden to its last line (after a quoted value only the quoted text is hidden); a key written with a backslash before its quote (JSON inside JSON) is covered by the rest-of-line rule. Error lines are redacted BEFORE they are cut to 300 / 200 characters or to their first line, so a token that straddles the cut leaves no head behind.
(v3.5b claimed percent-encoding but compared only against `encodeURIComponent(token)`, which is the token itself for the characters of a GitHub token: that claim was false until v3.5c, found by Codex on PR #390. v3.5c allowed the line break only after the prefix and underscore, which the README did not say: found by Codex on PR #391, fixed in v3.5d. v3.5d left a break inside a `%XX` escape as a listed residual; v3.5e closes it, and closes four more gaps found by a fresh adversarial pass that saw only the code and this paragraph: two tokens in a row, a shape behind a letter / digit / `_` / escaped newline, quoted Bearer values and other Authorization schemes, and wrapped or URL-encoded base64.)
Accepted residuals, stated so nobody relies on more. NOT hidden: a PLAIN space inside a foreign shape (after the underscore, in the prefix or in the body); a PLAIN space inside a `%XX` escape or between its hex digits; a lone CR, U+2028, a blank line (two breaks in a row), or a break followed by more than one space or tab as the gap; upper-case prefixes (`GHS_`, `GITHUB_PAT_`) and `github-pat_`; a `github_pat_` body that itself contains `gh?_`, where the tail from there is treated as a separate shape and stays visible if it is shorter than 16 characters; a shaped token longer than 255 characters leaves the tail past 255 visible; the base64 form leaves about four characters of its tail visible; a JSON-escaped newline (`\n` as two characters) or a `\uXXXX` / `%uXXXX` escape inside a token, a hex form, an HTML entity, a zero-width character inside a shape, more than three levels of percent escaping, and a reversed form are not recognised. Only the job token is matched character by character; any other credential is recognised only by the shapes and the Bearer / Authorization rules above. Also NOT hidden: a zero-width character between `Authorization` and its colon; the job token split by shell quoting (`'ab''cd'`) or joined with `+`; a percent-encoded header name (`authorization%3A...`); `Bearer` directly behind a letter, digit, underscore or escape; the part of an unquoted `Bearer` value after whitespace, a quote, a comma or a semicolon; a quoted value that contains a line break (only its first line is hidden); the text after a lone CR in a rest-of-line value; a zero-width character between `Bearer` and its value or inside the job token; a job token shorter than 8 characters (not redacted at all) and, for a job token longer than 256 characters, everything except its exact text (a GitHub installation token has 40). A job token that does not itself contain whitespace is matched by a direct scan, so the first redaction in a process takes a few milliseconds for a 40-character token and for a 100-character token. A job token that contains whitespace is still matched by a compiled expression, because the whitespace allowed between its characters has to share those characters with the token's own whitespace. Over-redaction near quotes is possible (for example `"token_type":"Bearer","access_token":...`). The first word of the line after a token that ended its line may be redacted with it. The runner's own masking of the job token remains a second layer, not a reason to print one. v3.5i: an `Authorization` key written with any number of backslashes before its quotes (JSON inside JSON, two or three levels) is now covered by the rest-of-line rule like the one-level form (the v3.5h rule allowed one backslash; found by the independent review, case 'Authorization esc2 json'). Accepted LOW residuals found by that review, each checked against the real `redact()` (the whole input printed back unchanged, the value visible): `Bearer%20<x>` (a percent-encoded space is not whitespace to the rule: `Bearer%20Sup3rS3cretV4lue`); `Bearer+<x>` (a plus is not whitespace: `Bearer+Sup3rS3cretV4lue`); a JSON key named `Bearer` or `bearerToken` (`{"Bearer":"Sup3rS3cretV4lue"}`: the rule needs `Bearer` followed by whitespace, `:` or `=`, and a key's closing quote is none of them); `xBearer <x>` (`Bearer` behind a letter is not matched, listed above as a word-boundary choice, `xBearer Sup3rS3cretV4lue`); `X-Auth-Token: <x>` and other custom credential headers (only `Authorization` and `Bearer` are named; any other credential is recognised by shape only); a full-width colon after `Authorization` (`Authorization` + U+FF1A + ` Basic Sup3rS3cretV4lue`: only the ASCII `:` and `=` count). Each costs one rule per spelling and would over-redact ordinary text; the runner's own masking of the job token is the second layer.
